    // About

    AI Technical Analyst & Full-Stack Builder

    I build AI workflows that take routine work off a person's plate and keep a human in charge. In this program I built nine: an inbox assistant that drafts replies in my voice and never sends, a design system that keeps everything I make consistent, and a college analysis that turned 200 schools into three clear comparisons. As a Technical Analyst, I care about the same thing in every build: it should work on a busy Monday morning, and someone should be able to trust it.

    // How I've used AI

    How I've used AI.

    It started with an exciting idea: “What if Claude already knew how I like things to look, how I write, and how I want my files handled?” So the first thing we built was a way for Claude to remember me.

    Phase one

    Identity & Voice

    We kicked things off with a custom Design System that carries my visual style into every new page, so everything matches from the start.

    From there came my favorite creation: the Voice Guide. After analyzing 20 of my actual emails, Claude drafted an 8-section breakdown of my tone (email-voice-guide.md). Today, an Email Manager uses that guide to write draft replies for my quick review and approval.

    Phase two

    System Orchestration

    Next, we expanded into a complete working environment, with analytical Spreadsheets, Presentations, project Context Files and a central Skills Library.

    To keep everything clean and safe, an audit-first File Cleanup utility makes sure every file change is reviewed and approved against a plan before it happens. And looking ahead, the same system is organizing my upcoming Zumba practice and routine planner. See what I'm automating next.

    // How I work

    Human in the loop.

    Three steps, every time.

    The same simple approach on every build, from the first conversation to the finished workflow.

    1

    Understand the people

    I start with the person doing the work, not the tool. What slows them down, and what would they hand off tomorrow?

    2

    Build the workflow

    Small, automated steps connected to the tools they already use, like Gmail, Calendar, Drive and Docs.

    3

    Keep a human in charge

    My assistants draft and suggest. Nothing gets sent or changed until a person has looked at it.
